subject.title: [Bug]: Documented channels.telegram.chunkMode / blockStreamingCoalesce rejected by plugin validator → gateway crash loop on restart — 2026.6.11

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the shipped documented flat `channels.telegram.chunkMode` and `channels.telegram.blockStreamingCoalesce` keys at validation time, or correct docs/doctor so only the nested `channels.telegram.streaming.*` shape is accepted?
rationale: The bug is user-visible and shipped docs advertised the flat keys, but current source and repository policy treat them as legacy config that should migrate through doctor rather than remain a steady-state runtime surface.

options.title: Compatibility repair
options.body: Accept or normalize the two documented flat keys now, add regression coverage, and update docs to steer future users to the nested canonical shape.

options.title: Docs and doctor only
options.body: Remove the flat-key docs and rely on `openclaw doctor --fix`, accepting that users who followed shipped docs need a manual recovery step.

options.title: Schema-only unblock
options.body: Land the open schema addition to stop the crash loop, then handle docs and doctor consistency in a follow-up.

recommendation.title: Compatibility repair
recommendation.body: Accept or normalize the two documented flat keys now, add regression coverage, and update docs to steer future users to the nested canonical shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on the canonical channel streaming config contract introduced in the config normalization work.
